messages.content: Use web search to find relevant datasets. Only include landing pages or DOIs. Do not invent links. Do not call time, date, timestamp, or clock tools.

Query: Can you find datasets about Employment, Community, urban and rural life, TRADE, INDUSTRY AND MARKETS, and Specific social services: use and availability in Lagos during the 1980s, matching this research need: Data on women in Ajegunle’s informal sector covering household living conditions, migration, housing, education, occupations, savings and union membership, finances, and income or business activities of shopkeepers, craftswomen, employed, and unemployed women.
Respond ONLY as JSON in this exact shape: {"items":[{"title":"...","url_or_doi":"...","justification":"..."}]}. Put any DOI, URL, landing page, or link in url_or_doi.

queries: Ajegunle women informal sector 1980s dataset shopkeepers craftswomen union savings Lagos
Ajegunle women informal sector survey 1980 Lagos household migration housing education data
action.query: Ajegunle women informal sector 1980s dataset shopkeepers craftswomen union savings Lagos

queries: "The Role of Women in the Informal Sector" "Ajegunle" dataset
action.query: "The Role of Women in the Informal Sector" "Ajegunle" dataset

content.text: {"items":[{"title":"The Role of Women in the Informal Sector: The Case of Ajegunle, Nigeria (GESIS Study ZA5003)","url_or_doi":"https://www.gesis.org/fileadmin/upload/forschung/publikationen/zeitschriften/za_information/ZA-Info-27.pdf","justification":"Excellent match and the most directly relevant historical dataset identified. Listed in the GESIS data archive under study number 5003. The study examines women's living conditions, occupational activities, and financial circumstances in Ajegunle, Lagos. Documented variables include household composition, marital status, housing conditions, rent, migration histories, education, occupations, food expenditure, bank accounts, savings associations, trade union membership, credit arrangements, and community services. It also investigates financial contributions, savings behavior, and economic activities among women in the informal sector. The linked 1990 GESIS archive publication confirms the dataset's existence, although it is not a direct microdata download page. This is the strongest candidate for obtaining the original historical survey data."},{"title":"The Informal Sector of Lagos: An Inquiry into Urban Poverty and Employment","url_or_doi":"https://ideas.repec.org/p/ilo/ilowps/991786423402676.html","justification":"Highly relevant historical survey of informal-sector enterprises in metropolitan Lagos, conducted during the 1970s and published as an International Labour Organization working paper in 1977. Covers enterprise ownership, business size, employment, labor supply, rural-to-urban migration, working hours, wages, and occupational training. Provides valuable baseline information for understanding women's informal employment, small businesses, trading activities, and economic conditions immediately preceding the 1980s. The linked record describes a sample survey, but the availability of original respondent-level data is not established."},{"title":"The Informal Sector of Lagos","url_or_doi":"https://books.google.com/books/about/The_Informal_Sector_of_Lagos.html?id=b-LSAAAAMAAJ","justification":"Relevant historical research containing statistical information on Lagos informal-sector enterprises, including Ajegunle. Covers household income, migration, education, employment, occupations, enterprise ownership, capital equipment, wages, economic activities, manufacturing, and retail trade. Useful for reconstructing the economic environment of Lagos during the late 1970s and early 1980s, particularly the employment opportunities and business conditions affecting women. This is a publication containing survey-based statistics rather than a confirmed downloadable microdata dataset."},{"title":"African Migrants in Lagos Suburbs: A Demographic and Socio-Economic Survey of Rural-Urban Migration in the Main Migrant Areas of the Federal Territory of Lagos, Nigeria","url_or_doi":"https://openresearch-repository.anu.edu.au/items/fe2138c0-eaeb-429d-9450-67d38bb83df9","justification":"Historical demographic and socioeconomic survey relevant to household living conditions, rural-to-urban migration, settlement patterns, and urban community life in Lagos. Examines migrant household heads, reasons for migration, socioeconomic characteristics, residential adjustment, and experiences of urban living. Particularly useful for contextualizing migration histories, household structures, and neighborhood development in Ajegunle. The survey predates the requested 1980s period and is not specifically focused on women informal-sector workers. The repository provides access to the research publication, not necessarily the original survey microdata."},{"title":"Living Conditions and Public Health Status in Three Urban Slums of Lagos, Nigeria","url_or_doi":"https://ir.unilag.edu.ng/items/92100e84-6612-4a30-ba77-a5ab9aa8de86","justification":"Directly relevant geographically because the underlying cross-sectional survey includes Ajegunle alongside Ijora Oloye and Makoko. The study surveyed 2,434 residents between June 2010 and October 2012, collecting information about demographic characteristics, migration histories, living conditions, and public health. Useful for investigating housing, household circumstances, and access to essential services in Ajegunle. Although substantially later than the 1980s, it offers comparative evidence for examining changes in neighborhood conditions. The repository record describes the survey findings but does not establish public availability of respondent-level data."},{"title":"The Millennium Development Goals in Lagos, Nigeria: A Time-Line Study of Ajegunle Community (1998–2008)","url_or_doi":"https://ir.unilag.edu.ng/items/c03eaaf0-1238-4e1c-a1e2-c3d35bd4b267/full","justification":"Ajegunle-specific longitudinal research based on household surveys conducted in 1998, 2002, and 2008, using systematic random sampling of 390 household heads. Examines socioeconomic characteristics, housing quality, neighborhood infrastructure, and settlement development. Relevant to community living conditions, housing, and the availability of basic services. Its repeated survey periods offer opportunities to study changes in Ajegunle after the 1980s. It is not a direct historical match, and the availability of original household-level data is unconfirmed."},{"title":"Urban Poverty and Environmental Conditions in Informal Settlements of Ajegunle, Lagos, Nigeria","url_or_doi":"https://www.academia.edu/17702597/Urban_Poverty_and_Environmental_Conditions_in_Informal_Settlements_of_Ajegunle_Lagos_Nigeria","justification":"Geographically specific survey-based research examining poverty, household income, housing, employment, and environmental conditions in Ajegunle. Reports occupational distributions across trading, artisanal work, civil service, farming, and fishing, alongside income patterns and neighborhood conditions. Relevant to reconstructing informal employment, household finances, and the availability of urban infrastructure and services. It also references earlier socioeconomic information from the 1990s. However, the underlying survey was conducted after the requested 1980s period, and the linked resource is a research publication rather than a confirmed microdata repository."},{"title":"The Home as Workplace: Investigating Home-Based Enterprises in Low-Income Settlements of the Lagos Metropolis","url_or_doi":"https://www.academia.edu/88245656/The_Home_as_Workplace_Investigating_Home_Based_Enterprises_in_Low_Income_Settlements_of_the_Lagos_Metropolis","justification":"Strong thematic match for women operating small businesses and informal enterprises from their homes. Survey-based research covering low-income Lagos neighborhoods, including Ajegunle, with information on gender, education, household size, housing tenure, employment, enterprise ownership, trading, manufacturing, business registration, savings, cooperative loans, rotating credit arrangements, and family financial assistance. Particularly useful for understanding the relationship between household living conditions and income-generating activities. The survey is considerably later than the 1980s, and the linked publication contains aggregate results rather than confirmed downloadable individual-level data."},{"title":"Socio-Economic Adaptation Strategies of the Urban Poor in the Lagos Metropolis, Nigeria","url_or_doi":"https://www.academia.edu/88245695/9adaptation_strategies_of_the_urban_poor_in_the_Lagos_metropolis_Nigeria","justification":"Relevant survey-based evidence on gender differences in informal-sector occupations, income, business ownership, household assets, and financing strategies. Based on 2010 fieldwork involving 396 respondents, including 183 women, across low-income Lagos communities that include Ajegunle. Provides sex-disaggregated information on trading, services, manufacturing, savings, rotating credit, cooperative financing, household income, and asset ownership. Particularly relevant to examining the financial practices of informal-sector businesswomen. It is useful for comparison with historical Ajegunle research, but does not provide 1980s observations or confirmed public access to individual-level records."}]}
